facts.text: Fairmead was founded in 1912 as Colony 13, a planned agricultural settlement by Cooperative Land and Title Company.
Mennonite farmers from Germany and Russia settled Fairmead, drawn by fertile soil and irrigation, shaping its early crop focus on alfalfa and dairy.
A creamery, cheese factory, lumber yard, and implement dealers sprang up quickly, supporting dairy production and general farming in the early years.
Fairmead sits at 253 feet elevation, 11 miles northwest of Madera, and its coordinates are 37°04′35″N 120°11′35″W.
The community’s soils are fine‑loamy Madera series with high clay, causing shrink‑swell and a water table that rises 3–6 feet in winter, leading to seasonal ponding.
Fairmead’s post office operated from 1913 to 1940, marking the town’s early communication link before the railroad era.
